quotes.text: Detached house, now in use as a convent. 1874-76 by R Norman Shaw for himself; northward extension at rear added 1885-86 by Shaw; minor additions 1892-93; later alterations. Red bricks (narrow bricks for main fronts, normal bricks at back) with rubbed brick hoods and aprons and enriched brick chimneys; some tile-hanging, wooden bargeboards, plaster ornament and render. Tiled roofs. White-painted timber windows of various types, most with leaded lights. STYLE: free Queen-Anne style. EXTERIOR: irregular south-facing front of three and four
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, opening paragraph and MATERIALS and STYLE headings (List Entry Number 1078274). The extracted span ends here mid-sentence; the word completing it sits in a second span and is not joined to this one.

quotes.text: Left-hand portion has boldly canted bay window rising through three storeys and crowned by a Chinese-style balcony (formerly timber, now iron) under a small dormer gable with tile-hanging and bargeboards. Right-hand portion has tiers of three 'Ipswich oriels' with plaster ornament between under a similar dormer gable. Tall, narrow windows in centre of various types, irregularly set. On the extreme right, single-storey entrance porch with rubbed brick surround to front (position of original entrance) and overhanging carved timber hood in style of Wren to return (current position of entrance). Tall, square stack right of centre on roof, with brick carving.

note: Tranche 3, British picturesque and Arts and Crafts cluster, 5 Sep 2026. Added as a new exemplar of `queen-anne-british`: the architect's own London house, and the one entry in this cluster where the register names the style in the node's own words -- 'STYLE: free Queen-Anne style'. It also states a distinction the node's kit could use and does not have: 'narrow bricks for main fronts, normal bricks at back', a brick module that changes with the face it is on.
